newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian minister in cash probe keeps party post.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian minister in cash probe keeps party post.

text.p: A top official in Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's political party, who faces trial for trying to leave Australia with a large sum of cash, refused on Monday to resign his party office.

Muhammad Muhammad Taib said at a news conference he would not resign as one of three vice presidents of the dominant United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) and asserted his innocence of the Australian charges.
Nevertheless, Muhammad resigned his post as Selangor chief minister at the weekend because of the controversy.

Muhammad was detained at Brisbane International Airport on December 22 after the equivalent of US$940,000 in cash was found in his luggage. He was later charged with failing to declare an amount over A$5,000.
On Friday, a court in Brisbane charged Muhammad on a second count for making a false declaration. His trial was fixed to begin on August 19.
Referring to his party position, Muhammad told reporters, "This is a post that I was elected to, so it's up to the party members to determine my position."

Speculation that Muhammad might resign from his party position cropped up after the announcement he was quitting his post as chief minister. Mahathir had said that UMNO members should be careful not to tarnish the party's name.
"I am not guilty, and I don't feel guilty," said Muhammad. He said the charges are technical in nature and that neither has to do with bribery or any similar offence.
"I will defend myself fully, and hopefully will redeem my good name," he said.

Mahathir announced Muhammad's resignation as minister after a leadership meeting of UMNO. He said the case had hurt the party's image. "Members should not smear UMNO's name by doing something which casts negative aspersions on the party," he said.
